direction: Keep the streaming text out of the spoken channel; announce a short status, then the full reply once.
dont_over_correct: Do not go silent: a page that announces nothing leaves a blind user not knowing a reply is coming (the status in rule 3 matters). Do not announce every sentence "to be safe", which brings back the chatter W3C warns about. Do not remove streaming for sighted users; this fix changes only what is spoken. Do not use `assertive` for ordinary replies.

prompt.not_applicable: The fix is enforced in the chat widget, not the prompt.

design: Put the status in its own region, in the page from the start.
While the reply streams, the reply body is not a live region.
Announce "Generating a response" once per reply
Expose the complete reply in one update
Announce failure once, as a complete message.
Test the live stream with the real screen readers

code.not_applicable: The fix lives in the chat widget; no package helper applies.

setup_questions: Can your agent supply these fields: reply.stream_start_ts, reply.stream_end_ts, live_region.writes, focus.changes, reply.length?
Where does the fix go in your agent: the chat widget?

evals.behaviour: Inspect the page before the first message: Put the status in its own region, in the page from the start
evals.pass_if: One empty `role="status"` element with `aria-live="polite"` is already present. A region created on the first reply fails.
evals.fail_if: No status region at load, a region added at the first reply, or the reply body used as the status

evals.behaviour: Do nothing special: ordinary reply is still spoken: Announce "Generating a response" once per reply
evals.pass_if: The same start status and one completion announcement. No extra speech, and no `assertive` interruption. Staying silent through the whole reply, with no status at all, is over-correcting and fails.
evals.fail_if: No start status, a repeat, or sentence-by-sentence updates

guardrail.not_applicable: The fix is in the chat widget's markup (live regions); the widget's accessibility test checks it, not a live check on the agent's replies.
